Actually, I recall that Anritsu Industrial Solutions Co., Ltd. is the successor name of Anritsu Infivis Co., Ltd. — the rename happened around April 2015.

But the rules here are strict: "spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity. ... Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

"Anritsu Industrial Solutions" vs "Anritsu Infivis" — these are not spelling drift or legal-suffix drift; they are genuinely different names. The issuing year in document context is 2015, and the rename occurred in April 2015 — but the register says "Anritsu Industrial Solutions". The certificate document itself says "Anritsu Infivis".

Given the rules, these are genuinely different names (not mere drift), so verdict = "different-entity", best_value = "Anritsu Infivis Co., Ltd." (the document's value, since the certificate is the legal instrument).

The why: The names are distinct corporate names (Anritsu Infivis vs Anritsu Industrial Solutions), not mere spelling/suffix drift, so the certificate's legal name prevails.
